subject: SLA proposal: split-coverage retainer & incident routing
messages:
From: Janelle Park <janelle@acme-commerce.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA inquiry for peak season coverage

Hi Olga,

We’re heading into our Q3 sales push and need clarity on support SLAs and pricing for higher-availability coverage. Two asks from my side: a) a short-term retainer option that buys guaranteed on-call coverage during our campaign (approx. 6 weeks) and b) a permanent uplift path if we decide to move to a tighter availability band (99.95%+).

Specifics: expected peak traffic May 15–June 30, primary region US, and we’ll need 24/7 on-call for Sev1 during the peak window. Please include how credits would be calculated for missed SLOs, any prorating rules for short-term retainers, and the ticket routing (who triages Sev1/Sev2 across Redwood’s teams).

Can you send a quick proposal and an example invoice calculation so I can prep procurement? Procurement timeline: signature by Apr 22 ideally.

Thanks,
Janelle
Janelle Park
Head of Platform Operations, Acme Commerce
Attachments: none
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Park <janelle@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-11T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA inquiry for peak season coverage

Hi Janelle — thanks for the clear ask. Draft proposal attached (Proposal_Acme_SLA_v2.docx) plus an export of the pricing sheet (SLA_pricing_table_v3.xlsx) and a one-page ticket routing matrix (Incident_Routing_Matrix.pdf). Key points up front:

- Short-term campaign retainer: $12,000/month (prorated daily) for a 6-week block. Covers 24/7 on-call routing for Sev1 incidents and a guaranteed 30-minute response target for Sev1 during the campaign.
- Permanent uplift path: baseline 99.9% included in standard plan. 99.95% add-on: +$5,000/month; 99.99% add-on: +$18,000/month.
- Credit calculation (summary): service credits are applied as % of the monthly retainer for the impacted component — example: for the short-term retainer, a single calendar-day outage classified as Sev1 causing availability below target triggers a credit of 10% of that retainer month’s fee (subject to a cap equal to 100% of the monthly retainer).
- Prorating rules: short-term retainers are charged pro rata by day; credit calculations use the pro-rated invoice period.
- Ticket routing: Sev1 -> Redwood on-call (24/7) -> escalation to SRE lead within 60 minutes if unresolved; Sev2 -> regional support hours (08:00–18:00 local) with next-business-hour response. Details in Incident_Routing_Matrix.pdf.

Questions I have for procurement to finalize pricing: do you require an explicit SLA credit multiplier for multi-region failover? Also, do you need a maximum monthly credit cap separate from the retainer cap? We can tailor that.

I’ll loop in Karthik to propose a final logged example invoice and amortization schedule so procurement has a table to sign off on.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Proposal_Acme_SLA_v2.docx, SLA_pricing_table_v3.xlsx, Incident_Routing_Matrix.pdf

Subject: Re: SLA inquiry for peak season coverage

Thanks Olga — adding the math/procurement-ready examples below so this can be dropped into Acme’s SOW quickly.

Short-term retainer example (6-week campaign, prorated):
- Daily rate = $12,000 / 30 = $400/day (we use 30-day month for quick math unless you want exact calendar-day prorate)
- Campaign length = 42 days -> prorated charge = $16,800 (billed once upfront or in two installments)

Credit example (single incident that breaches Sev1 target during campaign):
- If an incident reduces availability to 98.8% for a 24-hour window and that is classified under the campaign’s Sev1 SLO, the credit = 10% * prorated month equivalent. For a 42-day campaign billed as $16,800, the month-equivalent is $12,000 — credit = $1,200. Cap: 100% monthly retainer ($12,000).

Alternative: capped-tier model if Procurement requests a lower per-incident cap: we can set per-incident cap to 50% of monthly retainer with an aggregate monthly cap of 150% — we’ve rarely needed to apply more than one large credit in a month, but this gives procurement predictability.

Ticket routing summary (from the matrix):
- SEV1: Redwood on-call (PagerDuty) -> 24/7 -> SRE lead escalation after 60 minutes -> engineering hotfix channel.
- SEV2: Business-hours regional queue -> 4-hour response target -> escalation to ops lead if not acknowledged within 8 hours.

Optional add-on: a 2-week pre-launch dry run + on-call shadowing for $3,000 (recommended for campaigns where capacity spikes are expected). This reduces the likelihood of misclassification and speeds initial incident handling.

I’ve put the invoice rows in SLA_pricing_table_v3.xlsx and linked a sample amortization schedule in the shared drive. If procurement needs, Vanessa can seed the DocuSign with the SOW (we have a standard template to reduce review friction).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Olga & Karthik — this is exactly what procurement needed. A couple quick items:

1) Procurement prefers the two-installment billing (50% upfront, 50% at campaign midpoint).
2) We will accept the 100% monthly cap but please switch the per-incident cap to 50% with an aggregate monthly cap of 150% (Karthik’s alternate).
3) Please include the 2-week pre-launch dry run as an optional line item on the SOW; I’ll indicate acceptance if campaign metrics look good in the dry run.

Procurement timeline: legal review by Apr 18, signature by Apr 22. Can you send the DocuSign envelope and the final SOW with the adjusted caps and two-installment billing schedule? Also need a HubSpot deal link and final invoice rows for our AP team (PO will be generated once DocuSign is complete).

If you can get the DocuSign link today, I’ll route it through procurement immediately.

Best,
Janelle
